messages:
alex_h: quick heads-up — ran an ip exhaustion sim against prod-ish overlay tonight, and we hit >95% on ap-south-east-2-gpu-subnet-1 after simulating bursting pods + evict churn. sharing brief summary and a proposed tf change.

alex_h: TL;DR: bump that subnet from /24 -> /23 (secondary allocation) and add a low-risk canary that moves a single k8s node pool to the new subnet. plan attached. please skim: https://pr.internal/r/4523

maria_g: thanks. curious — did the sim include cross-AZ node recycling? that usually trips us up with ephemeral EIPs.

alex_h: yep included cross-AZ recycles + kubelet evictions (90s grace), and a synthetic load that spawns 6000 ephemeral pods over 30m. NAT eip usage peaked because kube-proxy recreated lots of hostNetwork pods.

samir_k: can you paste the terraform diff? want to make sure route tables and az allocations remain stable.

alex_h: sure — snippet from the plan:```hcl
# change to subnet CIDR
resource "aws_subnet" "gpu_subnet_1" {
  cidr_block = "10.40.0.0/23" # was /24
  map_public_ip_on_launch = false
}

# new attachment for canary
resource "aws_subnet" "gpu_subnet_canary" {
  cidr_block = "10.41.128.0/26"
}
```

maria_g: ok looks straightforward. two questions: 1) will expanding to /23 require re-creating the subnet resource (causing temporary detach)? 2) what's the impact on TGW route propagation?

alex_h: good call — AWS requires replacing for a CIDR change in that account; terraform will taint/create-new then migrate ENIs. plan shows: +/- 1 subnet replaced, ENI reassocs predicted but we can do in a maintenance window. TGW taught: we need to run a route table refresh job after cutover to ensure propagated routes show the new prefix.

ops_joanne: suggest we avoid recreating the subnet during peak. can we instead create the new /23 as an additional subnet and migrate prefixes? not sure AWS lets you overlap.

samir_k: you can't overlap. alternative: create new subnet in same AZ with /23 and migrate services off old to new (drain nodes) — more manual but zero replace. ops_joanne that is my preference.

maria_g: agree. plus add an automated verification step post-migration: check route table entries, TGW propagation, NAT gateway SNAT table size, and pod IP allocation success metric.

alex_h: plan update: create new subnet resource gpu_subnet_1b (/23) in same AZ, add to ASG/eks nodegroup, drain old nodes, then remove old subnet. PR updated at link above.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: checklist-4523 in #deployments. Steps: create subnet -> add to nodegroup -> canary drain -> full roll -> verify metrics -> remove old subnet.

ops_joanne: pinging security — will we need to open any additional SG rules? if ALB target groups or SG references used cidr block exactness, could break.

alex_h: I checked: we only reference subnets by id in TGW/ALB configs. SGs use ENI ids, so should be fine. will ping sec for a quick review.

samir_k: approve the approach. one nit: include `terraform state mv` commands in runbook to avoid losing state if resources get renamed during migration.

maria_g: +1. also add a smoke test: create a pod with hostPort + external egress and validate SNAT mapping post-migration.

alex_h: added both to the runbook. thanks all — i'll start the canary Wednesday 0300 UTC. will post results here and tag ops/security. :rocket:

ops_joanne: thanks — I'll schedule the maintenance window and loop in infra-sre. :calendar:
